architectural_fidelity.reason: Same room architecture preserved: white/neutral walls, ceiling height maintained, window position and size accurate, camera viewpoint and wide-angle perspective identical, beige carpet retained, door placement on left matches original.

furniture_removal.reason: All original furniture completely removed with no ghost outlines, remnants, or phantom shadows; clean base achieved throughout the space including where desk setup and bed were located.

style_commitment.reason: COVAJAPANDI style not executed with conviction; result is generic minimalist staging with low platform bed and mid-century credenza but lacks distinctive Japanese-Scandinavian fusion elements like shoji screens, natural wood warmth, textile layering, or cultural markers that define the style.

editorial_density.reason: Severely under-styled for editorial standards: only 2 small lamps, one credenza vignette with minimal styling, no wall art, single textile layer (duvet only), one small plant, no layered textiles, no rugs, no curated surface moments—falls far below Architectural Digest density.

photorealism.reason: Lighting coherent with natural window shadows, materials read as realistic (wood, fabric, carpet texture), no plastic CGI feel, shadows cast appropriately from furniture and window light.

designer_preference_reason: Collov delivers editorial-ready density with layered textiles, multiple art pieces, rich styling details, and complete room narratives that clients expect from professional staging, despite generic modern style.
what_cova_does_better: Maintains original architectural integrity more faithfully including wall color
Cleaner furniture removal with no artifacts
what_collov_does_better: Editorial-level styling density with multiple textile layers, wall art, plants, and accessories
Cohesive design story with curated vignettes throughout
Multiple light sources creating depth and interest
Lived-in luxury feel appropriate for high-end staging
specific_fixes_if_failing: Add wall art above bed—minimum large-scale piece or diptych/triptych arrangement
Layer textiles: add throw blanket, decorative pillows (minimum 3-4), area rug under or beside bed
Style credenza surface with books, decorative objects, and secondary plant
Add floor lamp or additional task lighting for layered illumination
Introduce COVAJAPANDI-specific elements: natural wood tones, wabi-sabi ceramics, minimal Japanese-inspired art, hygge textiles
Include reading chair or floor cushion to create secondary living zone
Add window treatment or shoji-inspired screen to reinforce style commitment
